The referer header is also interpolated into JavaScript; use URI(request.referer).origin and JavaScript-escape it.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate points out that request.referer is interpolated into JavaScript and recommends JavaScript-escaping it. That is the same unescaped-referer XSS concern raised in the golden comment, though the candidate's main focus is the postMessage origin problem.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw HTML cook method bypasses sanitization

Post#cook returns the post's raw HTML unchanged when cook_method is Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Imported embed/RSS posts are created with this cook method and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders post.cooked with `raw`, bypassing Discourse's sanitization. Any script, event handler, or dangerous URL in imported HTML can execute as stored XSS. Imported content must be sanitized or cooked through the safe pipeline.

RSS content is HTML-unescaped and then stored as raw HTML

Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML on feed item content and then imports it as raw HTML. This turns entity-escaped markup such as <script> into active HTML and stores it without sanitization, allowing stored XSS from an RSS/ATOM feed. Do not unescape feed content into raw HTML; sanitize or treat it as untrusted text.

Missing open-uri require for remote import

TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url) but the file does not require 'open-uri'. If open-uri has not been loaded by another code path, open will not understand HTTP(S) URLs and remote import will fail. Add require 'open-uri' and preferably use a hardened HTTP client.

import_remote fetches URL before validating scheme/host

TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read before validating that url is an allowed http/https URL. TopicEmbed.import only rejects non-http(s) URLs after the fetch, so untrusted URLs can cause open-uri to read local files or internal services. Validate scheme/host and use a hardened HTTP client before fetching.

Feed fetch has no timeout or size limit

poll_feed fetches the feed with open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and no open/read timeout or body-size limit. A slow or malicious feed can hang the Sidekiq worker or exhaust memory. Use an HTTP client with timeouts and a maximum response size.

Missing embed URLs can trigger full feed polling synchronously

TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) whenever feed polling is enabled and an embed URL is missing. This lets many unknown embed URLs on the allowed host trigger full feed downloads/imports synchronously, causing significant load and possible abuse. Feed polling should stay scheduled/globally debounced.

Throttle key set with separate SETNX and EXPIRE

TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? creates the Redis throttle key with setnx and then calls expire separately. If the process crashes between those calls, the key has no TTL and the URL is throttled forever. Use an atomic SET ... EX 60 NX operation.

content_sha1 updated even if post revision fails

When an existing embed's content changes, TopicEmbed.import calls PostRevisor#revise! and then updates topic_embeds.content_sha1 without checking whether the revision saved successfully. If the post update fails, the embed record is marked as up to date and future imports will skip it, leaving the SHA and post content inconsistent.

revise! returns true even when Post#save fails

PostRevisor#update_post ignores the return value of @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]), yet revise! returns true if the raw text changed. Callers can therefore believe a post was updated when it was not persisted. Check the save result and surface errors.

PostCreator side effects are not rolled back if TopicEmbed creation fails

TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create and TopicEmbed.create! in a Topic.transaction. PostCreator performs non-transactional side effects such as enqueuing jobs before TopicEmbed.create! runs; if TopicEmbed.create! fails, for example due to a uniqueness race on embed_url, the transaction may roll back the post while the enqueued jobs remain. Create/verify the embed record before triggering post-creation side effects or handle the race explicitly.

Migration uses create_table force: true, which drops existing data

The changed migration now creates top_topics with force: true. In Rails this drops the table if it exists before recreating it. If the table already exists in any environment, existing top_topics data can be destroyed. Use a guarded create_table or a separate migration.

New gems are not added to the Rails 3 lockfile

The Gemfile adds ruby-readability and simple-rss, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. When RAILS3 mode is used, Bundler uses the default Gemfile.lock; if that lockfile lacks the new gems, installation/booting will fail. Update all supported lockfiles or remove Rails 3 dual-boot support.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate downsize method definition silently removes width/height API

Ruby does not support method overloading. The second self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 overrides the previous self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145. The older width/height variant is dead code, and any existing caller using separate width and height arguments will now pass the height argument as opts, likely causing TypeError or wrong behavior. Remove the dead method or use a distinct method name if both signatures are needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem. The downsize method is defined twice, and the second definition (taking a dimensions string) overrides the first (taking max_width and max_height). This makes the original unreachable and breaks existing callers that pass separate width and height arguments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload size validation is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings

validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the limit depended on whether the upload was an image or attachment and on admin settings. The change replaces this with a constant 10 MB. Users can now select attachments or images larger than the configured limit (up to 10 MB), and the displayed 'file too large' error reports 10 MB even when the forum limit is lower or higher. Attachments are not downsized server-side by this PR, so this can bypass or confuse enforcement of attachment size limits.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate flags the same problem as the golden comment: the client-side limit is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores the per-type site settings (max_<type>_size_kb). This lets the client and server limits diverge. The candidate also notes the error message shows the wrong limit, which corresponds to the golden comment's point about the 413 handler.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsizing rewrites the same open Tempfile in place

OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) uses the same path as input and output for an external image tool while the Ruby tempfile object remains open. If the tool truncates, replaces, or renames the output file, the open file descriptor can point at stale data, so tempfile.size and later Upload.create_for may read the wrong bytes or an old inode. A failed conversion can also corrupt the only copy of the upload. Write to a separate temporary file and replace tempfile only after a successful conversion.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment says tempfile.size can return a stale cached value inside the loop, so the loop may never terminate. The candidate points at the same mechanism: the open tempfile descriptor goes stale after in-place downsizing, so tempfile.size reads wrong data. It frames the consequence as wrong bytes or corruption rather than a non-terminating loop, but the root cause is the same: tempfile.size is stale after modification.

false_positives.candidate:
413 upload error message uses hardcoded limit instead of site setting

When the server or web server returns HTTP 413, the alert now always says the maximum size is 10 MB. The previous code used Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb. If the configured limit or the web server limit differs, users receive an incorrect error message, making upload failures confusing and harder to diagnose.

API URL downloads are capped at 10 MB for all upload types, ignoring configured limits

FileHelper.download now always allows 10 MB, regardless of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb or attachment size limits. For images the PR attempts to downsize afterward, but for non-image attachments there is no downsizing step. This can permit or attempt uploads larger than admin-configured limits and increases resource usage by downloading oversized remote files.

Downsizing loop can stop while the image is still too large or conversion failed

The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and ignores the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails or five attempts are insufficient, execution still proceeds to Upload.create_for with a file that may exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The controller should verify the final size and return an error if it cannot reduce the file enough, rather than relying on later behavior.

Image processing command is executed via string interpolation without escaping

convert_with runs a shell command built from instructions.join(' ') using backticks. Paths are inserted as unquoted, unescaped arguments. The new automatic downsizing passes temporary file paths to this code; if a path contains spaces or shell metacharacters, the command can fail or execute unintended commands. Use system with an argument array or Shellwords.escape instead of interpolating into a shell string.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicsController#unsubscribe looks up TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately calls tu.notification_level. If the user has no topic_users row for that topic, tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError. The action should handle the missing record or use TopicUser.change, which creates the row when needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: tu is nil when no TopicUser record exists, so calling methods on it crashes with a NoMethodError.

false_positives.candidate:
State-changing unsubscribe is performed via GET

The /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe route is a GET route and TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately mutates TopicUser.notification_level. GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF tokens and can be triggered by link prefetching, email-client previews, or embedded resources while a user is logged in. Repeated GETs also move regular users to muted. Use a POST/PUT action with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation before changing state.

Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change and loses notification-change side effects

The action updates TopicUser with tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes; it sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change event. Bypassing it can leave client state stale and loses notification-change metadata.

track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id for non-User arguments

TopicUser.track_visit! assigns user_id as user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic. Callers such as TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic pass integer user ids, so the fallback uses the topic argument as the user id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user and corrupts per-user topic state. The fallback should be the user argument.

unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every use

The shared unsubscribe_link translation was changed to include %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder appends this translation whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any existing or plugin caller that enables add_unsubscribe_link but does not supply unsubscribe_url will fail interpolation or emit a broken link. Make the topic-specific line conditional on unsubscribe_url being present or update all callers.

Topic title is rendered unescaped with triple braces

The template renders {{{stopNotificiationsText}}}, and that property interpolates model.fancyTitle into an HTML string. Triple braces bypass Handlebars escaping, so any HTML in the topic title, or in a future representation of fancyTitle, would be injected into the page. Escape the title or render it through a safe component.

No meaningful coverage for the new unsubscribe behavior

The PR adds a state-changing unsubscribe endpoint and a new required unsubscribe_url interpolation, but the only spec change merely passes unsubscribe_url to Email::MessageBuilder and still only asserts the global preferences URL. There are no controller/request specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe, including missing TopicUser rows, notification-level transitions, slug redirects, or HTML/JSON behavior, and no spec asserting that the topic unsubscribe URL appears in email bodies or HTML.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty updateMany may not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. An empty Prisma updateMany payload is fragile: depending on Prisma behavior it may fail validation or not update the timestamp, defeating the stated intent and potentially causing webhook/cron errors. Pass an explicit updatedAt value, for example { updatedAt: new Date() }, and type the repository method with SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same problem: the empty data object passed to updateManyByCredentialId may not bump updatedAt. Both recommend the same fix, explicitly setting updatedAt.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook test script is not portable and uses fragile env path

The helper script uses BSD/macOS-specific sed -i '' and assumes ENV_FILE='../.env' relative to the current working directory. On Linux the sed command fails, and when run from the repository root the env path points outside the repo. Use a repo-root-relative .env path and a portable sed invocation.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says that the BSD/macOS-specific `sed -i ''` fails on Linux, which is the same issue as the golden comment. The extra point about the env path does not change that.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache deletion authorization only handles directly owned credentials

deleteCacheHandler authorizes only credentials where userId equals the requesting user. Connected calendars can include delegated credentials, as shown by the UI passing delegationCredentialId, and those may not be directly owned by the user. If such a credential has cache entries, the UI can show Delete cached data but the mutation will fail. Use the same access logic as credential deletion or explicitly authorize delegated/team credentials, and return a TRPC FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error rather than a generic Error.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate's main point is that delegated credentials are not authorized. It also explicitly recommends returning a TRPC FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error instead of a generic Error, which is the golden comment's concern. The golden issue is therefore covered, though only as a secondary point.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is always formatted with en-US

The cache timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') even though the component uses useLocale. Non-English users will see a US locale format. Use the active locale when creating the formatter.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same problem: the date is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' locale even though the component has the user's locale from useLocale. Both recommend using the active locale instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not refresh connected calendars

The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess; it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. After a successful deletion the tRPC cache still contains the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown continues to display the stale timestamp and may still show Delete cached data until a manual refetch. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query, preferably in onSuccess or onSettled.

Cache status includes expired cache rows

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache rows without an expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows where expiresAt >= now. Expired cache rows therefore still produce a cacheUpdatedAt value, causing the UI to report an active cache status and last-updated time for data that will not be used. Add expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } to the where clause.

credentialId input should be an integer

The input schema uses z.number(), which accepts floating-point values, but credential IDs are integer primary keys. Use z.number().int(), and optionally positive, so malformed input is rejected before reaching Prisma.

dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx runtime

dev:cron now runs npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not declared as a devDependency. This makes the script depend on npx downloading tsx at runtime, which is non-reproducible and can fail offline or in CI. Add tsx to devDependencies or keep using the already declared ts-node.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check is inverted for multiple intervals and ignores event end time

checkIfIsAvailable uses workingHours.find and marks the slot unavailable if any working-hours entry reports the slot outside that entry. With multiple working-hour entries on the same day, a slot that is valid in one entry is outside another, so it is incorrectly rejected. Additionally, end is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so slots that start inside working hours but end after working hours pass. The check should determine that the full slot is contained in at least one working-hours interval.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate states that the end is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, which is the same bug as the golden comment. It also raises a separate issue about multiple working-hour intervals, but the golden issue is still covered.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Day.js objects are compared with ===

The zero-length override check compares two Day.js objects with ===. This compares object identity and is always false for distinct Day.js instances, even if they represent the same instant. Use .isSame() if start and end equality is intended.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: Day.js objects compared with ===, which checks reference identity and so always returns false. Both recommend using .isSame() instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override path returns available without checking busy times

checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist when it sees any override on the slot's UTC date and, if the slot is not rejected by the override conditions, returns true before the busy.every() check. As a result, any busy periods or accepted bookings for that user are ignored for slots covered by a date override, so users can be offered and potentially book slots that are already busy.

Multiple date overrides for the same day are handled as mutually exclusive

The date override test uses dateOverrides.find and returns false when the slot is outside the iterated override. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the first override is outside the second, so find returns the second override and the slot is rejected. The correct condition is that the slot is inside at least one override, not outside any override.

Date override check allows slots that only partially overlap the override

The code treats a slot as outside an override only if slotEndTime is before or equal to the override start, or slotStartTime is after the override end. Therefore a slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is considered inside the override. For fixed-host round-robin availability this can expose slots when the fixed host is not available for the full event duration.

Override timezone conversion assumes optional timeZone is present

getSlots now reads override.timeZone to compute offsets, but TimeRange.timeZone is optional and no fallback is provided. If dateOverrides without timeZone are passed to getSlots, the offset calculation may use an unintended zone or fail depending on dayjs behavior. A fallback or required type should be used.

Missing tests for the fixed-host round-robin override behavior

The PR description says round-robin slots must respect fixed hosts' date overrides, but the added test only checks a personal event in another timezone. There is no regression test for round-robin with fixed hosts, multiple overrides, or busy times during a date override.

Fixed hosts list recomputed for every slot

Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for each slot. Since userAvailability does not change during the loop, this repeats work for every slot; compute fixedHosts once before filtering.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count is updated with a stale value instead of an atomic increment

Both failure paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If the same reminder is processed concurrently or updated between read and write, increments can be lost. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation instead.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same problem. retryCount is set from a stale read of reminder.retryCount + 1, which can lose increments under concurrency, and the fix is Prisma's atomic increment. It also covers both failure paths, matching the golden comment's note about the catch block.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry-count cleanup deletes workflow reminders of all methods

The deleteMany query deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount greater than 1 because the second OR branch does not include method: WorkflowMethods.SMS. This can delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or any future reminder type, even though the PR only intends to stop retrying SMS reminders. Add a method filter to the retry-count branch or make method a top-level AND condition.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the retryCount > 1 OR branch in deleteMany has no SMS method filter, so it deletes Email and WhatsApp reminders too.

false_positives.candidate:
Error handler can abort the whole cron batch if retry-count update fails

In the catch block, the retry-count update is not protected. If the reminder was deleted by another process or the database update fails, this update throws and terminates the handler, preventing the remaining reminders in the batch from being processed. Use updateMany or wrap this update in its own try/catch.

All exceptions count toward the SMS retry limit

The catch block increments retryCount for any exception thrown while preparing the SMS, including transient database errors, metadata validation errors, or template errors. After two such errors the reminder is deleted, even if the SMS provider was never contacted or the failure is transient. Consider counting only SMS provider failures or using a separate failure-handling path for unexpected errors.

Reminders with no message or destination are retried forever

When message is empty or sendTo is falsy, the code skips scheduling and does not increment retryCount. Such reminders remain unscheduled and are re-fetched on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which defeats the retry-limit behavior for permanently unsendable reminders. Consider incrementing retryCount, marking them cancelled, or deleting them after a failure threshold.

true_positives.golden_comment: Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Org scope skips org-member individual bookings when the org has no child teams

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition always includes the org id in teamIds, but it only fetches membership user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. For an organization with no child teams, userIdsFromOrg becomes empty, so individual bookings from org members are excluded. If at least one child team exists, org memberships are included. This makes org-scope visibility inconsistent. Query memberships for the org id and child team ids unconditionally.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the userIdsFromOrg fetch is guarded by teamsFromOrg.length > 0, so orgs without child teams leave out bookings from org members. Both also propose the same fix, querying memberships using teamIds (which includes the org id) without the guard.

false_positives.candidate:
Org/team raw SQL conditions are never executed against the database

The only actual database execution in this suite is the simple user-scope query. The org and team authorization paths generate array predicates and top-level OR conditions, but the tests only compare Prisma.sql fragment objects. That does not prove the generated SQL is valid or returns the correct rows. Add integration tests that execute getBaseConditions for team and org scopes against seeded bookings that should be included and excluded.

Public service API changed from findMany/Prisma where inputs to raw SQL fragments

The previous public findMany method is removed, and authorization/filter helpers now return Prisma.Sql instead of Prisma where input objects. Any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService will break unless updated. If this service is used elsewhere, callers need to be migrated in this change or a compatible query API should be preserved.

getBaseConditions can return an unwrapped top-level OR fragment

When there are no filter conditions, getBaseConditions returns authConditions directly. For org/team scopes this may be a top-level OR expression. If a caller composes the returned fragment with additional AND predicates, SQL operator precedence can change the meaning of the query. Return a parenthesized fragment or clearly document that the result must only be used as a complete WHERE clause.

Membership lookups do not use the injected Prisma client

The service receives a Prisma client and uses it for TeamRepository, but membership checks call static MembershipRepository methods without passing the injected client. If those static methods use a global/default client, authorization checks may run on a different connection, transaction, or read replica than the rest of the service. Pass the injected client to membership repository calls or confirm the static methods intentionally use the same client.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Placeholder refresh_token can overwrite real refresh token

If a refreshed token response does not include refresh_token, the code sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers that spread this parsed data into stored credentials, such as Office 365 and Zoom, can overwrite the real refresh token with this placeholder, permanently breaking future OAuth refreshes for that credential.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: when the refresh response lacks a refresh_token, it is set to the literal string 'refresh_token', which invalidates the real token and breaks later refreshes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

The minimum OAuth token schema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()], which evaluate to a literal string key rather than creating a Zod record/catchall. This means the schema does not accept arbitrary OAuth token fields and will reject normal refreshed token responses when app credential sharing is enabled, causing token refresh failures across affected apps.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the invalid computed keys [z.string().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema. The golden comment says this throws a runtime error, while the candidate says it creates literal keys and rejects valid responses. Both describe broken validation at the same spot, so the underlying issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google stores Zod SafeParse result instead of parsed credential key

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result, but GoogleCalendarService assigns that whole return value to key and saves it in credential.key. Subsequent credential reads will fail googleCredentialSchema.parse because the stored key is wrapped with success/data instead of containing the raw OAuth credentials.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse wrapper, and that wrapper is stored as the credential key instead of the parsed data.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without checking response.ok or parsing JSON, while callers expect different shapes: some expect a parsed token object, some an Axios response, and some a fetch Response. This inconsistency causes runtime crashes or corrupted credential updates in several app adapters and hides sync endpoint errors.

The sync helper returns the raw fetch Response when the credential sync endpoint is set, but callers expect integration-specific shapes such as res.data or a token object. That mismatch causes runtime errors in the sync-enabled path.

This skips required app-specific validation and transforms, for example Office 365's expires_in conversion, and can store unusable credential keys.

The normal Zoho CRM refresh path returns an Axios response with a data property, but when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. The code then reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and mutates zohoCrmTokenInfo.data, which will throw or corrupt token handling for Zoho CRM credentials.

SalesforceCalendarService calls prisma.credential.update but does not import prisma. This will throw a ReferenceError at runtime whenever Salesforce credential refresh attempts to persist the new access token.

The webhook handler performs findFirst followed by update or create without a transaction or unique constraint. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both find no existing credential and create duplicate credentials, leading to unpredictable app behavior and future updates only touching one duplicate.

When updating an existing credential, the webhook only writes key. If the credential was previously marked invalid, for example after an invalid_grant refresh failure, the newly synced valid credential remains marked invalid and may continue to be unusable.

The webhook secret header is compared to CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using !== instead of a constant-time comparison. For a secret-protected endpoint that can write OAuth credentials, a constant-time comparison is safer against timing-based secret leakage.

The endpoint should restrict this mutation to appropriate active booking statuses.

The organizer is loaded with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }). If a booking has no userId, which the fallback suggests is possible, this queries user ID 0 and throws, producing a server error instead of handling the booking gracefully. No capacity check for seat-limited events

The mutation adds attendees without checking booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot or the current attendee count. For event types with limited seats, a direct API call can overbook the booking by adding more attendees than the configured capacity.

Attendees are persisted before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called. If the calendar update fails, the API returns an error but the added attendees remain in the database, leaving the booking record and external calendar inconsistent. Consider transactional handling, compensation, or at least validating/preparing external updates before persisting.

This silently loses calendar events for secondary hosts.

Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer/eventType has no destination calendar

In handleNewBooking(), `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later collective-event merge uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when the value is null. Therefore team member calendars are ignored exactly in the case where the organizer has no destination calendar, defeating the purpose of supporting multiple host calendars.

Recurring cancellation ignores resolved credential and multiple calendar references

In handleCancelBooking(), when cancelling all remaining recurring events and a calendar reference has `credentialId`, the code resolves `calendarCredential` (possibly from DB) but then iterates only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` to delete events. It also finds only the first `_calendar` reference on each updated booking. For collective/multiple-host bookings, credentials not present on the organizer user or secondary calendar references can be missed or deleted with the wrong credential, leaving stale calendar events.

Paid cancellation does not await calendar deletion promises

In the paid booking cancellation branch, the code does `await apiDeletes;` where `apiDeletes` is an array of promises. Awaiting the array does not await the contained promises, so the handler can return before calendar deletions finish and the try/catch will not catch deletion failures. It should await `Promise.all` or `Promise.allSettled` on `apiDeletes`.

Recurring cancellation calendar deletions are not awaited or reliably collected

For recurring cancellations, the code calls credentials.filter(...).forEach(async ...), awaits getCalendar/deleteEvent inside the callback, and only then pushes the delete promise into apiDeletes. Because forEach does not await async callbacks, the handler can reach Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before those promises are pushed, so calendar deletions may not be awaited or included at all. This can leave cancelled recurring events in external calendars and cause unhandled rejections. Use a for...of loop or Promise.all over mapped credentials and await the resulting promises.

Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not wait for integration deletions

In the paid cancellation branch, `await apiDeletes;` awaits the array object rather than the promises inside it. As a result, deleteMeeting/calendar delete operations may still be pending when the handler returns, and their rejections are not observed. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` to wait for all integration deletion promises.

Video adapters are loaded sequentially

getVideoAdapters loops over credentials and awaits each appStore dynamic import one at a time. When multiple video credentials are present, this serializes module loading and delays availability checks, meeting creation, updates, and deletions. Use Promise.all to import the needed app modules concurrently.
